newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot natural gas prices tumble on weather.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natural gas prices tumble on weather.

text.p: Most Canadian spot natural gas prices tumbled in Wednesday trade as temperatures were forecast to climb in Alberta through Sunday.
The extent of the selloff surprised many traders.
"It's dropped like a rock," said one Calgary marketer. "It's going to be warm for at least five more days and people are realizing there's no market out there."

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was quoted at C$1.75/1.80 per gigajoule, down sharply from C$2.23/2.28 on Tuesday and C$2.60/2.65 last week. AECO gas for March delivery was quoted at C$1.85, down from C$2.25 from a week ago.

Environment Canada said temperatures in southern Alberta were expected to rise to 6 Celsius (43 Fahrenheit) by Sunday, which sources said prompted utilities to turn a cold shoulder to the spot market.
At Sumas, Wash., prices were talked in a wide range between US$1.80 and US$2.00 per million British Thermal units, down an average of 25 cents from last week.
One Vancouver trader said any gains that were expected from a return to full service of Northwest Pipeline on Wednesday were quickly erased by the weak Alberta prices.
In the east, gas in southern Ontario fetched about US$2.60 per mmBtu, down about 40 cents from February 5.
